Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Dormancy analysis must be complete and frozen by January 31 so due diligence can be mailed inside the Alabama 60-to-180-day pre-report window ahead of the before-May-1 life-company report; June 30 cut-off states run a parallel clock to the before-November-1 report

checklist.step: Fix the report-year cut-off and open the dormancy cycle
actions: Set the holder cut-off dates for the cycle: December 31 for the life writing companies (Ala. Code 35-12-76 life-company basis) and June 30 for any non-life holder entity in the group.
Confirm with the Statutory Reporting Manager the list of writing companies, FEINs and NAIC co-codes that must report, including dormant or run-off entities.
Open the dormancy workbook for the report year in the escheat folder named Escheat-<report year>-Dormancy and record the cut-off, entities and preparer.
Book the January 31 analysis freeze and February 15 sign-off dates into the escheat calendar and notify Operations so due-diligence mailing capacity is reserved.
checklist.done: the cycle workbook exists with cut-off dates, the full writing-company list and calendar milestones booked.

checklist.step: Refresh the 51-jurisdiction dormancy matrix with current statutory periods
actions: For each of the 50 states plus the District of Columbia, open the current holder reporting manual and record the dormancy period by property type: life insurance proceeds, matured endowment, annuity contract, retained asset account, uncashed drafts and outstanding checks.
Record Alabama at 3 years for insurance proceeds under Ala. Code 35-12-72 and capture the equivalent Arizona, California and Connecticut periods, which drive the largest owner populations.
Note the limiting-age trigger where the state deems a policy matured at the insured attaining the limiting age under the mortality table, and record that age.
Paste the statutory cite and the manual page date onto every matrix row — no row may carry a period without a source.
Publish the signed-off matrix to the escheat folder and email the version number to the Controller and Operations Manager.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction and property type has a dormancy period, a statutory cite and a dated source page in the matrix.

checklist.step: Extract uncashed claim and benefit drafts at the cut-off
actions: Run the outstanding-payments report as of the December 31 cut-off filtered to status Issued / Not Presented, excluding stop-paid and reissued items.
Pull for each draft: draft number, issue date, payee name, payee last known address, SSN or TIN where held, gross amount, claim or policy number and paying company.
Ask the Claims Director / Manager for the list of drafts under active dispute or litigation hold so they can be carried as documented exclusions rather than dropped silently.
Export to the dormancy workbook tab Drafts with the extract timestamp and row count in the header.
Reconcile the extract total to the outstanding-drafts liability balance in the GL and record the difference on the tab.
checklist.done: the Drafts tab holds every unpresented draft at cut-off with payee, address and amount, tied to the GL liability.

checklist.step: Extract stale outstanding checks and unapplied cash from the ledger
actions: Open the December bank reconciliation for every disbursement account and export the outstanding-items listing aged over 180 days.
Add the unapplied-cash and suspense account aging from the GL, filtered to items with no clearing activity since the cut-off minus 3 years.
For each item capture issue or receipt date, amount, remitter or payee, account code and the supporting document reference.
Ask the Treasury Analyst to confirm which accounts are in scope and which are internal transfer accounts that never hold owner property.
Load the result into the dormancy workbook tab Ledger and tie the total back to the reconciling-items balance.
checklist.done: aged outstanding checks and unapplied cash are extracted, tied to the bank reconciliation and loaded to the workbook.

checklist.step: Extract matured, limiting-age and terminated contract values from policy admin
actions: Run the contract status extract for policies with status Matured, Endowed, Terminated with Value or Death Confirmed and no disbursement recorded at cut-off.
Add contracts where the insured has attained the limiting age under the contract mortality table, using the ages recorded on the dormancy matrix.
Capture policy number, product, owner and beneficiary names and addresses, date of maturity or death, cash value or proceeds amount and the last owner-initiated transaction date.
Request from the Annuity Service Specialist the retained asset account balances with no owner-directed draft or statement acknowledgement in the same period.
Load to the workbook tab Contracts with row counts, and flag any contract missing an owner address for skip trace.
checklist.done: matured, limiting-age, death-confirmed and retained-asset balances are extracted with owner details and dates.

checklist.step: Extract premium credit balances and unrefunded overpayments
actions: Run the credit-balance aging by billing account as of cut-off, filtered to credits with no offsetting invoice and no owner contact for 3 years or longer.
Separate agent and broker commission credits from policyholder credits — they carry different NAUPA codes and different owner identification.
Capture account number, policyholder name and address, credit amount, credit origin (cancellation refund, duplicate payment, dividend) and last activity date.
Confirm with the Receivables Manager that none of the credits are held pending an agreed offset against another open receivable.
Load to the workbook tab Credits and reconcile the total to the credit-balance liability account in the GL.
checklist.done: aged policyholder and producer credit balances are extracted, categorised by origin and tied to the GL.

checklist.step: Assign a NAUPA property-type code to every row
actions: Open the NAUPA II property type code list and code each row: IN01 individual policy benefits, IN02 group policy benefits, IN03 proceeds due beneficiaries, IN06 unidentified remittances, IN07 other amounts due under policy terms, MS01 wages, CK01 cashier's cheques or the state's mapped equivalent.
Where a state publishes its own code crosswalk in its holder manual, record the state code alongside the NAUPA code on the row.
Reject rows that cannot be coded and send them back to the source-system owner for reclassification rather than defaulting them to a miscellaneous code.
Record the coder name and date on each tab.
checklist.done: every dormancy row carries a NAUPA property code and, where required, the state-specific code equivalent.

checklist.step: Establish the last-activity date that starts the dormancy clock
actions: Set the dormancy trigger date per property type: date of death for proceeds, maturity or limiting-age date for endowments, draft issue date for uncashed payments, last owner-directed transaction for retained asset accounts and credit balances.

Override the trigger where evidence of owner interest exists — a signed change of address, a premium payment, a portal login recorded in the customer self-service audit log, or a returned call logged in the service system.
Reject system-generated events (automatic dividend postings, statement mailings, index credits) as owner activity, because most RUUPA states do not count them.
Document the evidence reference for every overridden row so the reset can be defended in an examination.
checklist.done: each row carries a defensible dormancy trigger date with owner-activity evidence cited where the clock was reset.

checklist.step: Apply the priority rules to assign each row to a jurisdiction
actions: Apply the first priority rule from Texas v. New Jersey: report to the state of the owner's last known address as shown in the holder's books and records.
Where no address exists or the address is a foreign country, apply the second priority rule and assign the row to the state of incorporation of the writing company.
Standardise addresses through the reference data service before assigning, so a mis-keyed state code does not send property to the wrong administrator.
Count the rows falling to second priority and report the count to the Controller — a rising count signals a data quality problem, not a windfall.
Write the assigned jurisdiction and the priority rule applied onto every row.
checklist.done: every row is assigned to a jurisdiction with the priority rule and the address source recorded.

checklist.step: Run the dormancy clock and flag the reportable population
actions: Join each row to the dormancy matrix on assigned jurisdiction plus NAUPA property code to pull the statutory period.
Compute dormancy expiry = trigger date + statutory period, and flag Reportable where dormancy expiry falls on or before the December 31 cut-off.
Produce a second flag, Maturing, for rows expiring within the following 12 months so Operations can pre-clean the addresses.
Summarise the reportable population by jurisdiction, property code, item count and dollar value on the workbook Summary tab.
Spot-check 20 rows by hand against the matrix and record the check in the tab footer.
checklist.done: the Reportable and Maturing flags are set on every row and the Summary tab totals by jurisdiction and property code.

checklist.step: Document every exclusion from the reportable population
actions: List on the Exclusions tab every row removed from the population with the reason: reissued or voided draft, active claim dispute or litigation hold, court-ordered interpleader, IRS levy or garnishment, or business-to-business exemption where the state grants one.
Cite the statutory basis for each exemption class — B2B exemptions differ sharply between states and none may be assumed to apply nationally.
Attach the supporting evidence reference (case number, void confirmation, court order) to each excluded row.
Total the excluded dollars and present them to the Controller separately from the reportable total.
checklist.done: no row leaves the population without a named exclusion reason, a citation and an evidence reference.

checklist.step: Reconcile the dormancy population back to the general ledger
actions: Tie the total of the Drafts, Ledger, Contracts and Credits tabs to the corresponding GL liability and suspense account balances at cut-off.
Explain every reconciling difference in writing: items below reporting thresholds, excluded rows, timing of post-cut-off clearings.
Post the escheat liability reclassification entry moving reportable balances into the unclaimed-property payable account, referencing the workbook version.
Have the Controller review the entry and the reconciliation before the population is frozen.
checklist.done: the reportable population reconciles to the GL with every difference explained and the reclass entry posted.

checklist.step: Search for prior-year property that was never reported
actions: Compare this year's population to the prior three years' filed reports and isolate items whose dormancy expiry pre-dates the last filed report year.
For each, determine the missed report year, the jurisdiction, the aged balance and the interest or penalty exposure under that state's act.
Take the exposure to Regulatory Counsel and decide in writing between reporting it as a late item on the current report or entering the state's voluntary disclosure agreement programme.
Log every prior-year item in the regulatory issue tracker with the missed year, the state and the chosen disposition.
checklist.done: every unreported prior-year item is quantified, logged and has a written counsel-endorsed disposition.

checklist.step: Freeze the analysis and obtain Controller approval
actions: Review the Summary tab against the prior year by jurisdiction and property code and challenge any movement over 25% in count or value.
Confirm the GL reconciliation, the exclusion log and the prior-year catch-up log are all complete before signing.
Sign and date the workbook cover sheet, lock the workbook to read-only and issue it as version FINAL to Operations for due-diligence mailing.
Notify the Head of Compliance and the Chief Financial Officer of the total reportable value and the number of owners in writing.
checklist.done: a signed, locked FINAL dormancy analysis is issued to Operations by January 31 with the totals communicated to Finance leadership.

checklist.step: File the dormancy evidence package for the retention period
actions: Deposit the locked workbook, all source extracts with row counts, the dated dormancy matrix, the GL reconciliation and the Controller sign-off into the repository under Escheat / <report year> / Dormancy.
Apply the 10-year retention label measured from the report filing date so the package survives the state examination look-back.
Confirm the index makes the package searchable by report year, jurisdiction, writing company and NAUPA property code.
Record the repository reference on the escheat calendar entry for the year.
checklist.done: the complete dormancy package is filed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by year, state and property code.

testing.step: Build an independent population of potentially dormant items
actions: Pull directly from the GL, without using the escheat team's workbook, every outstanding disbursement, credit balance and suspense item open at the December 31 cut-off aged over three years.
Add an independent policy-admin extract of matured, limiting-age and death-confirmed contracts with no disbursement, and the claims payment register of unpresented drafts.
Reconcile your extract counts and totals to the account balances in the trial balance and clear any difference before proceeding.
Sign the extract as complete, recording the query, run date and row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: an auditor-built population exists, reconciled to the trial balance and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the auditor population to the escheat team's dormancy analysis
actions: Match your population to the FINAL dormancy workbook on draft number, policy number or GL document number.
List every item present in your extract but absent from the workbook, and every workbook item absent from your extract.
Trace each unmatched item to either the documented Exclusions tab or a genuine omission — an item sitting in neither is an automatic exception.
Quantify the omitted dollars by jurisdiction and flag any single omission over $25,000 for immediate escalation.
testing.done: the two populations are reconciled item by item with every difference either evidenced as an exclusion or raised as an omission.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of items over $25,000 and 100% of rows assigned to a jurisdiction under the second priority rule.
Take 45 further rows by seeded random selection stratified across Drafts, Ledger, Contracts and Credits, minimum 60 rows in total.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add 10 rows drawn from the Exclusions tab so exclusions are tested, not trusted.
testing.done: a reproducible, stratified sample is drawn covering high-value, second-priority and excluded rows.

testing.step: Re-perform the dormancy period lookup against the statute
actions: For each sampled row, open the assigned state's current holder reporting manual and read the dormancy period for that property type yourself before looking at the matrix.
For Alabama rows confirm the 3-year insurance-proceeds period at Ala. Code 35-12-72 and the December 31 life-company report basis at 35-12-76.
Compare your reading to the matrix value; a right period supported by a wrong or stale citation is still an exception.
Capture the manual page you relied on, dated, into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independent dormancy-period conclusion with a dated source capture.

testing.step: Recompute the dormancy expiry maths on the sample
actions: Recompute dormancy expiry = trigger date + statutory period for every sampled row using your own formula, not the workbook's.
Compare the Reportable flag you derive to the flag on the workbook row and list every disagreement.
Pay particular attention to rows expiring within 60 days either side of the cut-off, where an off-by-one-year error moves property between report years.
Report the recomputation error rate against the 2% threshold.
testing.done: expiry dates and Reportable flags are recomputed for the whole sample and the error rate is stated against the threshold.

testing.step: Challenge the trigger date and any owner-activity reset
actions: For sampled contract rows, open the policy record and confirm the date of death, maturity date or limiting-age date used as the trigger matches the system record.
For every row where the clock was reset for owner activity, open the cited evidence — signed address change, premium payment, logged inbound call — and confirm it is genuine owner-initiated contact.
Reject resets based on system-generated events such as automatic dividend postings, index credits or outbound statement mailings.
Recompute the expiry without the disputed reset and quantify the property that should already have been reported.
testing.done: every sampled trigger date is confirmed to source and every unsupported activity reset is reversed and quantified.

testing.step: Re-perform the jurisdiction assignment under the priority rules
actions: For each sampled row, read the owner's last known address as it appears in the source system, not in the workbook, and derive the first-priority state yourself.
For rows assigned under second priority, confirm the books and records genuinely hold no usable address and that the state of incorporation used is the writing company's, not the group parent's.
Flag any row where an address exists in an adjacent system — the claims file, the billing account or the service correspondence log — but was not used.
Quantify the value that would move between administrators if the assignment errors were corrected.
testing.done: sampled jurisdiction assignments are independently derived and any misdirected value is quantified by state.

testing.step: Test the exclusions and the property-code assignments
actions: For each sampled excluded row, read the cited statute or exemption and confirm it covers that property type in that state — treat a B2B exemption asserted nationally as a fail.
Open the supporting evidence (void confirmation, court order, litigation hold notice) and confirm it is dated before the cut-off.
Check the NAUPA property code on sampled reportable rows against the code list and the state crosswalk, since a wrong code drives the wrong dormancy period.
Treat any exclusion reading only 'not escheatable' with no citation as a fail rather than a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled exclusion is supported by a state-specific citation and dated evidence, and property codes are confirmed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception recording the item reference, jurisdiction, dollar value, what was wrong and the report year affected.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: source extract incomplete, stale dormancy matrix, wrong property code, unsupported activity reset, address not sourced, exclusion unsupported.
Name an owner and a remediation date, and for omitted prior-year property open a voluntary disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next report year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue reference, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the omission value and the sample error rate and compare them to the zero-omission and 2% thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the reviewer, who neither prepared the dormancy workbook nor any source extract, sign and date the workpaper.
File the workpaper under Escheat / <report year> / Testing and table the results and any voluntary-disclosure exposure at the next Audit Committee sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the omission value and the error rate, and the committee reporting date is recorded.

checklist.step: Receive the frozen dormancy population and open the mail cycle
actions: Take the FINAL locked dormancy workbook from the Controller (Escheatment) and confirm the version and sign-off date before loading it.
Load the Reportable rows into the due-diligence case queue keyed by owner, property reference, assigned jurisdiction, NAUPA code and amount.
Reconcile the loaded case count and value back to the workbook Summary tab and record the tie-out in the cycle log.
Book the mail-run capacity with the print vendor and record the planned drop dates per state window.
checklist.done: the case queue is loaded, reconciled to the signed workbook and mail-run drop dates are booked per state.

checklist.step: Build the per-state threshold and mailing-window table
actions: For each of the 51 jurisdictions, record from the current holder manual the due-diligence value threshold, the earliest and latest mailing dates relative to the report deadline, and the required mail class.

Record Alabama as $50 and not more than 180 nor less than 60 days before filing per Ala. Code 35-12-79, and capture California's separate second-notice requirement and Connecticut's certified-mail trigger.
Compute the concrete window open and mail-by calendar dates for this report year from each state's report deadline and put them on the row.
Note states that require the notice to be sent by first-class mail only and states that permit or require electronic notice where the owner consented.
Publish the table to the escheat folder with citations and email the version to Operations and the print vendor coordinator.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction row shows the threshold, concrete window dates, mail class and citation for this report year.

checklist.step: Refresh and validate owner addresses before mailing
actions: Run the full mailing file through USPS NCOALink for move updates and CASS standardisation and record the coverage percentage.
Submit owners with no address, a foreign address or an NCOA nixie result to the LexisNexis batch search using name, SSN or TIN and prior address to obtain a current address.
Cross-check against the claims file, the billing account and the service correspondence log for any newer address the escheat extract did not carry.
Update the case record with the refreshed address, the source and the refresh date — never overwrite the original address, keep both.
Report the address-refresh coverage against the 98% target to the Operations Manager before the print file is cut.
checklist.done: every mailable owner has a standardised, refreshed address with the source and date recorded, and coverage is reported.

checklist.step: Apply the threshold and determine who must be noticed
actions: Join each case to the threshold table on assigned jurisdiction and compare the property value to that state's threshold.
Aggregate multiple properties held for the same owner in the same state before applying the threshold, because states test the owner's total, not the item.
Mark below-threshold cases as No Notice Required with the state and threshold cited on the case, and keep them in the population for aggregate reporting.
Produce the eligible-owner count and value by state and send it to the Compliance Analyst for a second check before printing.
checklist.done: each case is marked notice-required or below-threshold against a cited state threshold, with owner-level aggregation applied.

checklist.step: Assemble the statutory letter content and get it approved
actions: Confirm each template carries the mandatory elements: owner name, the property description and amount, the property reference, a statement that the property will be transferred to the named state administrator if the owner does not respond, the response deadline, and the holder contact name, telephone number and mailing address.
Add the state-specific wording each administrator prescribes, including the administrator's name and the statutory cite, and the Spanish-language version where the state requires it.
Confirm no template asks for information the company does not need — a due-diligence letter is not a data-collection exercise and must not request full SSN in the clear.
Sign and date each state template version and lodge it in the document repository as the approved artwork for the cycle.
checklist.done: every state letter template is counsel-approved, dated and versioned with all mandatory elements present.

checklist.step: Set the mail class per case and flag certified items
actions: Default the mail class to first-class mail with an ancillary endorsement so undeliverables are returned with the reason.
Flag for certified mail with return receipt every case where the state requires it above a stated value — commonly $1,000 or more — reading the value from the threshold table.

Where the state permits electronic notice and the owner has a recorded, verified email consent, queue the email as an addition to, not a replacement for, the paper letter unless the statute allows substitution.
Send the certified list to the mailroom separately with the required article numbers pre-assigned.
checklist.done: every case carries a mail class consistent with its state's rule and certified items are separately queued with article numbers.

checklist.step: Produce and drop the mail run inside the statutory window
actions: Merge the approved template with the case data and generate a PDF letter per owner, indexed to the case and property reference.
Proof 25 merged letters against source cases for name, amount, property description, administrator name and response deadline before release.
Release the print file to the vendor and require a postal acceptance manifest showing the drop date and piece count per state.
Confirm the drop date sits on or after the window open date and on or before the mail-by date for every state in the run, and hold back any state that would fall outside.
Archive the letter images and the acceptance manifest against each case.
checklist.done: letters are merged, proofed, dropped inside every state's window, and the acceptance manifest is archived per case.

checklist.step: Open and staff the inbound response channel
actions: Stand up a dedicated escheat response queue with the telephone number printed on the letters and route it to trained agents.
Brief agents with the call guide: how to verify the caller, what the letter means, what the owner must supply, and the promise that no fee is charged to reclaim property.
Configure the queue to disposition every contact against the owner's case reference so responses reconcile to the mailing file.
Set the response SLA at 5 business days to first substantive action and alert daily on breaches.
Forecast volume from last cycle's response rate so the queue is staffed for the fortnight after each drop.
checklist.done: a dedicated, staffed and scripted response queue is live from the drop date with case-level dispositioning and an SLA.

checklist.step: Work owner responses through to payment or reactivation
actions: Verify the responding owner or beneficiary against the policy or payment record using knowledge-based identity checks before discussing amounts.
Collect what the payment requires: current address, tax identification, a completed claim or reissue form and, for a deceased owner, a certified death certificate and proof of beneficiary status.
Instruct Treasury to issue the reissued draft or claim payment and record the payment reference on the case.

Where the owner confirms interest but the payment cannot be completed before the report freeze, record the documented owner contact as an activity reset and take the case out of the report with the evidence attached.
Close the case with a disposition of Paid, Reactivated, Owner Declined or No Response.
checklist.done: every response is identity-verified, dispositioned and either paid, reactivated with evidence, or returned to the report population.

checklist.step: Work returned and undeliverable mail
actions: Scan every returned envelope against its case, capturing the postal return reason: attempted not known, moved left no address, insufficient address, deceased.
Submit moved and insufficient-address cases for a second skip trace and re-mail inside the window if calendar time allows.
Route returns marked deceased to the death-verification queue rather than straight to escheat, so a beneficiary claim can be opened.
Record the return, the re-trace outcome and any re-mail on the case, and mark cases with no deliverable address as Report Without Address.
checklist.done: every returned piece is scanned to its case with a reason, re-traced where possible, and re-mailed or marked undeliverable.

checklist.step: Reconcile the mailing file against the eligible population
actions: Tie the acceptance manifest piece counts per state to the eligible-owner counts per state and explain every difference.
List any eligible owner with no letter, establish why, and either mail inside the remaining window or raise an exception if the window has closed.
Produce the response summary: letters mailed, responses received, dollars paid or reactivated, cases still reportable, by state.
Send the reconciliation and summary to the Controller (Escheatment) as the input to the report build.
checklist.done: letters mailed reconcile to eligible owners state by state and the reduced reportable population is handed to the Controller.

checklist.step: Release reactivations and payments out of the escheat population
actions: For every case dispositioned Paid or Reactivated, reverse the escheat liability reclassification and post the payment or the return to the original liability account.
Attach the case reference and the owner evidence to the journal so the reversal can be traced in an examination.
Reconcile total reversals to the reduction between the frozen dormancy total and the final reportable total.
Confirm no case appears both as paid and as reportable before the report is built.
checklist.done: all paid and reactivated cases are reversed out of the escheat liability and reconciled to the reduction in the reportable total.

checklist.step: Escalate suppressions, late runs and undeliverable-only owners
actions: Review every case suppressed from the mail run and require a written reason — duplicate owner, litigation hold, confirmed fraud, prior opt-out — before approving the suppression.
Approve or reject any state mail run that missed its window, and where it missed, decide in writing whether to re-notice next cycle and hold the property or report it with a disclosed notice failure.
Sign off the population being reported without a deliverable address and confirm a second skip trace was attempted on each.
Record every decision with date and rationale on the cycle log.
checklist.done: every suppression, late run and undeliverable-only owner has a dated, written management decision on the cycle log.

checklist.step: Report the outreach outcome to Compliance and Finance
actions: Publish the cycle dashboard: letters mailed by state, response rate, dollars returned to owners, undeliverable rate and average days to pay.
Compare response and undeliverable rates to the prior two cycles and explain any movement over 5 percentage points.
Flag any state where the undeliverable rate exceeds 10% as a data-quality remediation item back to the source system owner.
Present the dashboard at the Compliance Committee alongside the escheat report totals.
checklist.done: the outreach dashboard is published, benchmarked against prior cycles and presented with remediation items named.

checklist.step: File the due-diligence evidence for the retention period
actions: Deposit per-owner letter images, the postal acceptance manifests, certified-mail receipts, the returned-mail log, response dispositions and the reconciliation into Escheat / <report year> / Due Diligence.
Apply the 10-year retention label measured from the report filing date so evidence survives the state examination look-back.
Confirm the index allows retrieval by owner name, property reference, jurisdiction and drop date, which is how examiners sample.
Record the repository reference on the cycle log and close the cycle.
checklist.done: the full outreach evidence set is filed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by owner and property reference.

testing.step: Rebuild the eligible-owner population independently
actions: Take the FINAL dormancy workbook, aggregate property to owner within each state, and apply each state's threshold from the statute yourself to derive who was notice-eligible.
Confirm you used the same frozen workbook version the Operations team loaded, by matching version number and sign-off date.
Reconcile your eligible-owner counts and values by state to the counts Operations reported and clear every difference.
Sign the population as complete with the derivation query and run date in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently derived eligible-owner population exists, reconciled by state to the operations figures.

testing.step: Reconcile letters actually mailed to the eligible population
actions: Match every eligible owner to a letter image and a line on the postal acceptance manifest.
List eligible owners with no letter image and letters with no matching eligible owner in either direction.
Confirm the manifest piece counts per state equal the number of letter images per state — a manifest without images is not proof of mailing.
Treat any threshold-eligible owner with no mailed letter as an automatic exception with no materiality filter.
testing.done: every eligible owner is matched to a letter image and a manifest line, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of certified-mail cases and 100% of owners with property over $25,000.
Take 50 further owners by seeded random selection stratified across the five highest-volume states plus a random spread of the remainder, minimum 70 owners in total.
Add 10 suppressed cases and 10 returned-mail cases so the exception paths are tested.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible stratified sample is drawn covering certified, high-value, suppressed and returned-mail cases.

testing.step: Recompute the mailing window against each state's statute
actions: For each sampled owner, read the assigned state's current notice provision and derive the window yourself — for Alabama, not more than 180 nor less than 60 days before the report filing date under Ala. Code 35-12-79.
Recompute the window open and mail-by dates from the state's actual report deadline for this cycle.
Compare the postal acceptance date on the manifest to your recomputed window and count the days on both edges.
Any letter dropped before the window opened is as much a fail as one dropped after the mail-by date — both can invalidate the notice.
testing.done: each sampled letter's drop date is tested against an independently recomputed window with day counts documented.

testing.step: Inspect letter content against the statutory required elements
actions: Open the actual merged letter image for each sampled owner, not the blank template.

Confirm it names the owner, describes the property and amount, states that the property will be delivered to the named state administrator if the owner does not respond, gives the response deadline, and gives a holder contact name, telephone and address.
Confirm the state-prescribed wording, administrator name and statutory cite are present and current for that state, and that any required Spanish version accompanied it.
Check no letter requests a full SSN in the clear or implies a fee is payable to recover the property.
testing.done: every sampled letter image is confirmed to carry all statutory elements and correct state-specific wording.

testing.step: Verify the address used was the best address available
actions: For each sampled owner, confirm an NCOA and CASS pass was run and the refresh date pre-dates the drop date.
Search the claims file, billing account and service correspondence log for any address newer than the one printed on the letter.
For owners with no address, confirm a LexisNexis skip trace was attempted and its result is attached to the case.
Flag every letter mailed to a stale address when a newer one existed in an adjacent system, and quantify the affected value.
testing.done: address refresh is evidenced for each sampled owner and every avoidable stale-address mailing is flagged and quantified.

testing.step: Trace certified-mail proof and returned-mail handling
actions: For every certified case, locate the article number, the acceptance record and the return receipt or the tracking outcome.
Confirm certified mail was used wherever the state's value trigger applied and that no qualifying case went by first-class only.
For sampled returned-mail cases, confirm the return reason was recorded, a second trace was attempted, and deceased returns were routed to death verification rather than straight to escheat.
List any qualifying case with no certified proof as an exception.
testing.done: certified proof exists for every qualifying sampled case and returned mail is evidenced as re-traced or correctly routed.

testing.step: Re-perform response handling and removal from the report
actions: For sampled cases dispositioned Paid or Reactivated, trace to the payment reference or the documented owner-contact evidence and confirm the case is absent from the final report population.
For cases dispositioned Reactivated with no payment, confirm the owner contact was genuine and documented — a returned call with no owner verification is not a reset.
Confirm the GL reversal exists for each paid case and matches the amount removed from the escheat liability.
Check no sampled case appears both as paid and as reported to a state, which would create a double payout exposure.
testing.done: each sampled response disposition traces to payment or documented owner contact and to a consistent report and GL position.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the owner reference, state, property value, and whether the defect invalidates the notice.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: window missed, threshold misapplied, letter content deficient, address not refreshed, certified rule missed, suppression unsupported.
Name an owner and a remediation date, and where notice was invalid decide with Regulatory Counsel whether to hold the property and re-notice next cycle.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a re-notice decision where notice failed.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report before the filing
actions: Compute the notice-coverage percentage, the window-compliance percentage and the undeliverable rate against the 100%, 100% and 10% thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the reviewer, who sits outside Operations and approved neither the templates nor the mail run, sign and date the workpaper.
Issue the conclusion to the Controller (Escheatment) before the report is filed so failed states can still be re-noticed, and file the workpaper under Escheat / <report year> / Due Diligence.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states coverage, window compliance and undeliverable rates, and reaches the Controller before filing.

checklist.step: Freeze the post-due-diligence reportable population
actions: Take the Operations reconciliation of letters mailed, responses paid and cases reactivated and apply it to the frozen dormancy population.
Produce the final reportable population by jurisdiction, writing company and NAUPA property code with owner-level detail.
Tie the final total to the frozen dormancy total less paid and reactivated cases, and record the bridge in the cycle log.
Lock the population as REPORT BASIS <report year> and issue it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager; no row may be added after this point without a documented late-item entry.
checklist.done: a locked report basis exists, bridged from the dormancy total through paid and reactivated cases, and issued for build.

checklist.step: Confirm each jurisdiction's deadline, form and submission channel
actions: For each of the 51 jurisdictions record from the current holder manual the report due date, the as-of date, the required file format, the submission portal URL and the accepted remittance methods.

Record Alabama as report and remit before May 1 on the December 31 life-company basis under Ala. Code 35-12-76 and 35-12-77, and record California's split notice-report and June remit-report cycle explicitly, since it needs a second submission.
Record which states require a negative report when there is nothing to report and which do not want one filed at all.
Record each state's extension policy and the date by which an extension must be requested.
Load every date onto the filing calendar with T-45, T-21, T-10 and T-3 alerts.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction has a recorded due date, format, portal, remittance method, negative-report rule and calendar entry.

checklist.step: Refresh holder registrations and portal credentials
actions: For each state portal confirm the holder account is active for every reporting writing company under its own FEIN and holder identification number.
Register any newly reporting entity, including run-off and merged companies, and record the assigned holder ID against the entity.
Reset expiring credentials and confirm at least two named users can submit for each state so a single absence cannot miss a deadline.
Update the holder contact of record — name, title, telephone, email and mailing address — because deficiency notices go there.
checklist.done: every reporting entity has an active holder account and holder ID on every state portal with two credentialed submitters.

checklist.step: Map the report basis into the NAUPA II record layout
actions: Map each owner row into the NAUPA II layout: HOLDER record with FEIN, name and contact; PROPERTY records with owner name, address, SSN or TIN, relationship code, property type code, date of last activity and amount reported; and the TOTALS record.
Populate relationship codes correctly — sole owner, beneficiary, joint owner, estate — because they drive how the administrator publishes the property.
Carry the policy or draft number into the property description field so the administrator can match a claimant back to the company record.
Build one file per state per writing company, named <state>-<FEIN>-<report year>.
Record the file row counts and totals for the pre-submission reconciliation.
checklist.done: a NAUPA II file exists per state per entity with complete holder, owner, property and totals records and recorded control totals.

checklist.step: Apply aggregate reporting and owner-detail rules
actions: For each state read the aggregate threshold from the holder manual and roll only properties below it into a single aggregate line where the state permits it.
Never aggregate where the owner name and address are known and the state requires detail — aggregating away a known owner defeats the reunification purpose and draws examiner findings.
Retain the owner-level detail behind every aggregate line in the workpaper, because states can request it years later.
Record the aggregate threshold applied and the count and value aggregated per state.
checklist.done: aggregation is applied only where permitted, owner detail is retained behind every aggregate line, and thresholds are documented.

checklist.step: Protect owner PII in the submission package
actions: Confirm SSN and TIN fields are populated only where the state requires them and are transmitted only through the state's encrypted portal upload or its published secure transfer method.
Reject any state process that would require emailing an unencrypted owner file and use the portal or an encrypted transfer instead.
Confirm the files at rest in the escheat folder are stored in the restricted-access area with access limited to the reporting team and audit.
Log the transfer of owner PII to each administrator in the processing record.
checklist.done: owner identifiers are present only where required, transmitted encrypted, stored restricted and logged as a disclosure.

checklist.step: Validate the files and clear every reject
actions: Run each file through the state's validation utility or the portal's pre-submission validator and export the error report.
Fix the common rejects at source rather than in the file: invalid property type code for the state, missing date of last activity, malformed SSN, unbalanced totals record, invalid state abbreviation.
Re-run validation until the file passes clean, and keep the first and final validation reports as evidence of the correction.
Escalate any state whose file cannot be made to pass by T-21 to the Regulatory Reporting Manager so an extension can be considered while there is still time to request one.
checklist.done: every file passes the state validator clean and the validation reports before and after correction are retained.

checklist.step: Prepare negative reports and confirm entity coverage
actions: List every writing company and state combination with no reportable property this year.
For states that require a negative report, prepare and queue it for the same deadline as a positive report.
For states that do not want a negative report, record that fact with the manual citation so the absence of a filing is explainable at examination.
Confirm no entity has silently dropped out of the filing set compared with last year without a documented reason such as a merger.
checklist.done: every entity-state combination is either a positive filing, a queued negative report, or a cited no-filing-required position.

checklist.step: Reconcile the files to the report basis and the general ledger
actions: Sum the NAUPA file totals by state and by entity and tie them to the locked report basis with a zero variance requirement.
Tie the aggregate of all state totals to the unclaimed-property payable balance in the GL and explain any residual, which should consist only of items not yet dormant.
Prepare the remittance schedule by state showing the amount, the payment method and the payment date targeted ahead of the due date.
Present the reconciliation and remittance schedule to the Controller for approval.
checklist.done: file totals tie to the report basis with zero variance and to the GL payable, and a remittance schedule is prepared.

checklist.step: Obtain Controller approval of the remittance before funds move
actions: Review the remittance schedule against the prior year by state and challenge movements over 25% in value or owner count.
Confirm the reconciliation shows zero variance between filed totals and the report basis before approving.
Approve the total remittance and the per-state amounts in writing and release the schedule to Treasury.
Confirm the funding account has cleared balance to cover the full remittance on the earliest payment date.
checklist.done: the per-state remittance is approved in writing with funding confirmed, ahead of the earliest state due date.

checklist.step: Submit each report through the state's portal and capture the confirmation
actions: Log in to each state's holder portal with the entity's holder ID, upload the validated NAUPA file and complete the online holder verification or affidavit where the state requires one signed by an officer.
Submit no later than the T-3 business day alert so a portal outage on the due date does not cause a late filing.
Capture the confirmation number, submission timestamp and any receipt PDF for every filing, positive and negative.
Where a state still requires a paper cover sheet or a notarised verification, print, sign, notarise and mail it by tracked post and keep the tracking number.
Record the confirmation number against the state row on the filing calendar the same day.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction shows a submission timestamp and confirmation number on or before its statutory due date.

checklist.step: Remit the funds and match every payment to its filing
actions: Execute the approved remittance by each state's accepted method — ACH debit initiated in the portal, ACH credit to the administrator's account with the required addenda, or cheque where the state still demands it.
Include the holder ID, report year and confirmation number in the payment reference so the administrator can match funds to the report.
Confirm each debit or cleared cheque against the bank statement and record the value date on the state row.
Chase any state whose payment has not cleared within 10 business days rather than assuming it landed.
checklist.done: every state's remittance is executed, referenced to its filing and confirmed cleared on the bank statement.

checklist.step: Relieve the payable and post the accounting entries
actions: Post the entry relieving the unclaimed-property payable for the amount remitted per state, referencing the confirmation number.
Post separately any interest or penalty paid so it is visible as a cost of non-compliance rather than buried in the remittance.
Prepare the account reconciliation showing the payable roll-forward: opening balance, additions from the dormancy analysis, releases from paid and reactivated owners, remittances and closing balance.
Have the Controller review and certify the reconciliation in the close tool.
checklist.done: the payable is relieved per state, interest and penalties are shown separately and the roll-forward is certified.

checklist.step: Work administrator confirmations, deficiency notices and claims
actions: Track receipt of each administrator's acknowledgement and chase any state silent after 10 business days using the portal message centre.
Work every deficiency notice within the state's stated response window, correct the underlying record and file the amended report where required.
Route owner claims that the administrator forwards back to the company for verification to the service team and answer within the administrator's deadline.
Record each notice, response date and outcome on the state row so a pattern of deficiencies in one state becomes visible.
checklist.done: every state has an acknowledgement or a worked deficiency, and forwarded owner claims are answered within the administrator's deadline.

checklist.step: File the filing evidence package for the retention period
actions: Deposit the submitted NAUPA files, validation reports, confirmation receipts, signed verifications, remittance advices, bank clearing evidence and the payable roll-forward into Escheat / <report year> / Filing.
Apply the 10-year retention label measured from the filing date, matching the examination look-back most states assert.
Confirm the index supports retrieval by state, writing company, confirmation number and owner name, which is how an examiner will sample.
Close the cycle on the filing calendar and open the next report year.
checklist.done: the filing package is complete, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by state, entity and owner.

testing.step: Build the complete filing inventory for the report year
actions: List every writing company and every one of the 51 jurisdictions as a required cell, so a missing filing shows as a gap rather than being invisible.
Populate each cell from the filing calendar with the filing type (positive, negative, none required), due date, submission timestamp and confirmation number.
Compare the entity list to the statutory annual statement filing list to confirm no reporting entity was omitted.
Sign the inventory as complete and record any cell you could not populate.
testing.done: a full entity-by-jurisdiction inventory exists with every cell populated or flagged as unpopulated.

testing.step: Reconcile filed amounts to the report basis and the general ledger
actions: Sum the submitted NAUPA file totals by state and compare to the locked report basis, requiring zero variance at state level.
Tie the aggregate remitted amount to the unclaimed-property payable relief postings in the GL for the period.
Trace the payable roll-forward from opening balance through dormancy additions, paid and reactivated releases and remittances to the closing balance.
Investigate any residual payable balance and confirm it consists only of property not yet dormant, not property that should have been remitted.
testing.done: filed totals, remitted funds and GL relief reconcile at state level with the residual payable explained.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Test 100% of jurisdictions for filing existence and timeliness — with 51 cells there is no reason to sample that attribute.
For detail testing take the 10 highest-value states plus 10 states selected at random by a recorded seed.
Within each selected state draw 15 owner records by seeded random selection from the submitted file.
Record the seed, the population sizes and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: all 51 jurisdictions are covered for timeliness and a reproducible owner-level sample is drawn across 20 states.

testing.step: Recompute every due date and measure filing timeliness
actions: For each jurisdiction read the current statute and holder manual and derive the due date and as-of date yourself.

Confirm Alabama on the December 31 life-company basis with a before-May-1 report and remit date under Ala. Code 35-12-76 and 35-12-77, and confirm California's separate June remit-report submission was made as well as the notice report.
Compare the recorded submission timestamp to your derived due date and record the days early or late for every cell.
Treat any filing submitted after the due date without an approved, dated extension on file as a fail and compute the interest and penalty exposure under that state's act.
testing.done: due dates are independently derived for all 51 jurisdictions and timeliness is measured with late-filing exposure quantified.

testing.step: Verify each submission actually landed with the administrator
actions: For each sampled state open the holder portal submission history under the entity's holder ID and read the status and confirmation number directly.
Compare the portal record to the confirmation stored in the evidence repository — an internal screenshot is not proof that the state accepted the file.
Confirm the file the portal shows as accepted matches the file version retained internally by row count and total.
For paper-verification states, trace the tracked-post receipt for the signed and notarised cover document.
testing.done: each sampled filing is confirmed accepted in the state's own portal record and matched to the retained file version.

testing.step: Re-perform owner-level detail from the filed file back to source
actions: For each sampled owner record trace name, address, property amount, date of last activity and property type code back to the policy, claim payment or GL source record.
Confirm the relationship code reflects the real relationship — beneficiary property reported as sole owner will not reach the right claimant.
Confirm the property description carries the policy or draft number so an administrator can match a claimant back to the company.
Flag every field discrepancy and assess whether it would prevent the administrator reuniting the owner with the property.
testing.done: every sampled owner record is traced to source with field discrepancies flagged and their reunification impact assessed.

testing.step: Test aggregation and negative-report positions
actions: For sampled states read the aggregate threshold from the holder manual and confirm nothing above it was aggregated.
Open the detail behind each aggregate line and confirm no property with a known owner name and address was aggregated where the state requires detail.

For every cell recorded as negative report or no filing required, confirm the manual citation supports it and, where a negative report was required, confirm it was submitted with a confirmation number.
List each unsupported aggregation or missing negative report as an exception.
testing.done: aggregation limits and negative-report positions are independently confirmed against each sampled state's manual.

testing.step: Trace remittance from the filed report to cleared funds
actions: For every jurisdiction match the reported total to the payment initiated and to the bank debit that cleared, including value date.
Confirm the payment reference carries the holder ID, report year and confirmation number so the administrator could match funds to the report.
Identify any state reported but not remitted, or remitted in an amount different from the filed total, and treat either as a fail regardless of size.
Confirm interest and penalties paid were posted separately and were approved by the Controller.
testing.done: reported and remitted amounts agree state by state with cleared bank evidence and correctly referenced payments.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the state, entity, amount, days late where applicable and the quantified interest and penalty exposure.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: deadline missed, validation reject unresolved, entity omitted, aggregation misapplied, remittance mismatch, portal registration lapsed.
Name an owner and a remediation date, and for late or missed filings agree with Regulatory Counsel whether a voluntary disclosure agreement or penalty-abatement request is the right route.
Carry every open exception into the next report year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, quantified exposure, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a counsel-endorsed route.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute filing completeness and timeliness across all 51 jurisdictions and the report-to-remittance variance, against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind every finding.
Have the reviewer, who built no report, validated no file and holds no payment release authority, sign and date the workpaper.
File under Escheat / <report year> / Filing and report completeness, timeliness and penalty exposure to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states filing completeness, timeliness and remittance variance, and the committee reporting date is recorded.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Case-level alerts at day 45 and day 75 of the 90-day validation clock, a quarterly alert 15 days after quarter end if the comparison has not run, and a pre-cut-off alert each December for confirmed deaths not yet claimed
