Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A skipped quarterly comparison, a match left unvalidated past 90 days, or a confirmed death with no beneficiary outreach is logged with the policy count, the face amount exposed and the market-conduct reporting implication

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Claims Officer signs off every match closed as not-a-death and every confirmed death closed without a paid claim before it is referred to escheat

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All in-force individual and group life policies, annuity contracts and retained asset accounts on the quarterly comparison extract, plus every DMF match generated and its disposition

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of in-force records must appear on the comparison extract — any excluded product line or legacy administration system is a fail; 100% of matches must be dispositioned within 90 days; a false-negative found in the re-run sample fails the matching criteria and forces a full re-run

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation runs quarterly; the test runs quarterly on that quarter's comparison, with an annual extended test each Q4 that re-runs matching over the full in-force file to hunt false negatives

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside claims operations and must not have dispositioned any sampled match

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly DMF comparison test workpaper (extract reconciliation, match sample, re-run results, 90-day clock recomputation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Escheat / DMF / <year>-Q<n>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Comparison run log by quarter, DMF file versions used, match volumes and dispositions, and per-policy validation and beneficiary outreach evidence, producible for a multistate unclaimed life insurance benefits examination within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager fronts multistate examination and data-call responses on unclaimed life benefits; Regulatory Counsel clears any statement about historic non-comparison or missed matches before it is filed

checklist.step: Define the quarterly comparison scope and build the in-force extract
actions: Extract as at quarter end every in-force individual life policy, group life certificate, annuity contract and retained asset account, including paid-up, reduced paid-up, extended term and premium-waiver contracts.
Include contracts lapsed within the look-back the company applies, because a death before lapse can still create a claim.

Capture per record: policy or contract number, insured and annuitant full name, SSN or TIN, date of birth, gender, issue date, status, face amount or account value, and beneficiary details where held.
List every administration platform in the group, including legacy and acquired-block systems, and confirm each contributed rows — a silent legacy system is the classic examination finding.
Record the extract date, per-system row counts and the total on the run log.
checklist.done: the extract covers every administration platform with per-system row counts recorded and no product line silently omitted.

checklist.step: Obtain the current Death Master File and record its version
actions: Obtain the SSA Death Master File through the company's certified subscription — the full file plus every weekly and monthly update issued since the last comparison.
Record the file version, issue date and record count on the run log so the comparison can be reproduced exactly.
Confirm the update files have been applied cumulatively so no death window is skipped between quarters.
Store the file in the restricted-access area with the DMF use restrictions applied, since it carries protected identifiers.
checklist.done: the DMF full file plus all interim updates since the last run are loaded, versioned on the run log and stored restricted.

checklist.step: Standardise names, dates and identifiers on both sides
actions: Normalise names on both files: strip titles and suffixes, split compound and hyphenated surnames, and hold nicknames against a standard variant table so Bob and Robert can match.
Standardise dates of birth to a single format and flag placeholder values such as 01/01/1900 that would create spurious matches.
Validate SSN format, strip formatting characters and flag records with no SSN so they route to name and date-of-birth matching instead of dropping out.
Produce a data-quality report showing the percentage of in-force records with a usable SSN and with a usable date of birth, and send it to the Operations Manager.
Log every standardisation rule applied so the same rules can be re-applied in testing.
checklist.done: both files are standardised under logged rules and the usable-identifier coverage is reported before matching runs.

checklist.step: Run the exact-identifier match
actions: Run the exact match on nine-digit SSN plus surname, and separately on SSN alone, and output both result sets.
Retain the DMF date of death, reported state and file version on every hit so the dormancy clock has a source date.
Count hits by product line and administration platform and compare to the prior quarter — a platform producing zero hits two quarters running is a defect signal, not good news.
Write the exact-match output to the match case queue with a match category of EXACT.
checklist.done: exact SSN matches are produced with date of death and DMF version attached and loaded to the case queue.

checklist.step: Run the fuzzy match categories on records without an exact hit
actions: Apply the model comparison categories on the residual population: surname plus first name plus date of birth exact; SSN match with a name variation; date of birth match within a stated tolerance with name match; and transposition-tolerant SSN comparison.
Allow common data defects to still match — transposed date-of-birth digits, maiden versus married surname, missing middle initial, transposed SSN digits.
Score every candidate and route scores above the review threshold to the case queue as category FUZZY, and hold the rest in a reviewable near-miss file rather than deleting them.
Record the criteria version and thresholds used on the run log so the run is reproducible.
checklist.done: fuzzy candidates are generated under the recorded model criteria, scored, queued for review, and near misses are retained.

checklist.step: Triage the match queue and suppress prior dispositions
actions: Deduplicate matches where one insured holds several contracts so the case is worked once but each contract is tracked.
Suppress matches previously dispositioned as not-a-death with evidence, but re-open any suppression older than two years for re-check.
Exclude contracts where a death claim is already open or paid, and record the claim number on the case as the reason.
Set the 90-day validation clock on every remaining case starting at the match run date, and record the due date on the case.
checklist.done: the queue is deduplicated, evidenced suppressions applied and every open case carries a dated 90-day validation due date.

checklist.step: Complete the good-faith effort to confirm the death
actions: Search the LexisNexis person report for the insured to corroborate the death: date of death, obituary, last known address and surviving relatives.
Where the record is ambiguous, order a certified death certificate from the state vital records office of the DMF-reported state of death.
Attempt contact at the last known address and telephone number on the policy record and log every attempt with date and outcome.
Confirm or reject the death in writing on the case with the evidence attached — never close a match as not-a-death on a hunch or a single failed telephone call.
Where confirmed, record the date of death on the policy record, which starts the dormancy clock for escheat.
checklist.done: each match is confirmed or rejected in writing with attached evidence, and confirmed deaths carry a date of death on the policy.

checklist.step: Identify and locate the beneficiaries
actions: Read the current beneficiary designation from the contract file, including any assignment, trust, collateral assignment or change of beneficiary endorsement.
Where the beneficiary is deceased or unnamed, work the contingent beneficiary and then the contract's default order — estate, spouse, children — and document the chain applied.
Search for current beneficiary addresses through the LexisNexis batch service and the company's other customer records.
Where no beneficiary can be identified or located, document each search attempt, because that documentation is what supports escheating the proceeds later.
Record the identified beneficiaries and addresses on the case.
checklist.done: every confirmed death has an identified beneficiary chain with current addresses or a documented, dated failure to locate.

checklist.step: Send the claim packet and work the claim
actions: Send each located beneficiary a claim packet: covering letter naming the policy and insured, claimant statement, tax election form and instructions on the proof of death required.
Open a claim in the claims system referencing the DMF case so the two records stay linked.
Follow up at 30 and 60 days where no claim form is returned, and log every contact attempt.
Compute and add any interest payable on delayed death proceeds under the applicable state's prompt-payment provision from the date of death.
Pay the claim on receipt of a complete packet and record the payment reference back on the DMF case.
checklist.done: each located beneficiary has a claim packet, a linked claim record, logged follow-ups and either a payment or an open claim.

checklist.step: Refer unclaimed confirmed deaths into the escheat population
actions: List every confirmed death where no beneficiary was located, no claim was returned, or the beneficiary declined, together with the proceeds amount and the confirmed date of death.
Hand the list to the Controller (Escheatment) for inclusion in the dormancy analysis, with the date of death as the dormancy trigger date.
Confirm the receiving analyst has the beneficiary search evidence, because the escheat file must be defensible without re-opening the claim.
Reconcile the referred count and value against the case queue so no confirmed death is stranded between claims and escheat.
checklist.done: every unclaimed confirmed death is referred to escheat with its date of death and search evidence, and the handover reconciles.

checklist.step: Handle inbound lost-policy and administrator claimant enquiries
actions: Answer NAIC Life Insurance Policy Locator requests forwarded by the states within the service standard, searching the same in-force and terminated files used for the DMF comparison.
Answer state administrator enquiries where a claimant has found the property on a state's unclaimed property site and needs the company to confirm entitlement.
Where a locator or administrator enquiry finds a policy the DMF comparison did not flag, raise it as a matching defect, not just a service case.
Log every enquiry, response date and outcome so response times can be evidenced at examination.
checklist.done: locator and administrator enquiries are answered within standard and any miss by the comparison is raised as a matching defect.

checklist.step: Close the quarter and report the comparison metrics
actions: Publish the quarter's metrics: in-force records compared by platform, exact and fuzzy match counts, deaths confirmed, beneficiaries located, claims paid with value, cases referred to escheat and cases still open past 90 days.
Compare match rates by platform and product line to the prior four quarters and explain any fall of more than 20%.
Escalate every case still open past the 90-day clock with a named owner and a recovery date.
Present the pack to the Compliance Committee and to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for data-call readiness.
checklist.done: quarterly metrics are published, benchmarked against four quarters, with every over-90-day case escalated and owned.

checklist.step: Review and approve the closed-as-not-a-death population
actions: Review the list of matches closed as not-a-death and confirm each carries corroborating evidence, not merely a failed contact attempt.
Challenge any platform or product line with an unusually high not-a-death rate, since that pattern usually means poor identifiers rather than living insureds.
Approve the closures in writing with date, or send cases back for further validation.
Approve every confirmed death referred to escheat without a paid claim, confirming the beneficiary search was genuine.
checklist.done: all not-a-death closures and unpaid confirmed deaths carry a dated executive approval before the quarter is closed.

checklist.step: Tune the matching criteria and re-run where a defect is found
actions: Analyse confirmed deaths that the comparison missed and were found by a locator request, a beneficiary call or a later quarter, and identify which criterion failed.
Adjust thresholds or add a variant rule, document the change with its rationale and version it on the criteria record.
Re-run the amended criteria over the current in-force file and quantify the additional matches produced.
Where the change produces material additional matches, run it over the prior two years of in-force files and treat the output as a remediation population.
checklist.done: every known miss is traced to a criterion, the criteria are versioned, and material changes trigger a back-run remediation.

checklist.step: File the comparison evidence for the retention period
actions: Deposit the in-force extract manifest, the DMF file version record, the match output with scores, validation evidence, beneficiary outreach letters and claim outcomes into Escheat / DMF / <year>-Q<n>.
Apply the 10-year retention label so the evidence survives a multistate unclaimed life insurance benefits examination look-back.
Confirm the index supports retrieval by policy number, insured name, match category and quarter, which is how an examiner samples.
Record the repository reference on the quarterly run log and close the quarter.
checklist.done: the quarter's comparison evidence is filed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by policy, insured and quarter.

testing.step: Rebuild the in-force comparison population independently
actions: Extract in-force counts by product line and administration platform at quarter end directly from each system, without using the operations extract.
Reconcile your counts to the in-force exhibit in the statutory annual statement and to the policy counts in the actuarial valuation file.
List every platform, legacy block and acquired block, and confirm each appears on the operations extract with a comparable row count.
Sign the population as complete with the queries, run dates and counts recorded in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independent in-force population exists, reconciled to statutory and valuation counts, covering every platform.

testing.step: Reconcile the operations extract to the independent population
actions: Compare your counts to the operations extract row counts by platform and product line and explain every difference.
Investigate any product line, block or platform absent from the comparison and quantify the face amount not compared.
Confirm paid-up, reduced paid-up, extended-term and retained asset records are in scope, since these are the classic silent omissions.
Treat any in-force population excluded from the comparison as an automatic exception irrespective of size.
testing.done: the operations extract is reconciled platform by platform with any uncompared population quantified as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of matches with a face amount over $100,000 and 100% of matches closed as not-a-death.
Take 40 further matches by seeded random selection stratified across EXACT and FUZZY categories and across platforms, minimum 60 in total.
Add 25 non-matched in-force records selected at random for false-negative testing.
Record the seed, population sizes, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible stratified sample is drawn covering high-value, not-a-death, matched and non-matched records.

testing.step: Re-run the matching criteria independently
actions: Load the same DMF file version recorded on the run log and re-run the exact SSN match yourself over the independent in-force population.

Re-run the fuzzy categories using the documented criteria — name plus date of birth, SSN with name variation, date-of-birth tolerance, transposition tolerance — and compare your candidate set to the operations output.
Investigate every candidate you produced that the operations run did not, since these are potential false negatives.
Test the sampled non-matched records for a death present in the DMF and treat any hit as a matching failure requiring a full re-run.
testing.done: matching is independently re-performed on the same DMF version and every extra candidate and false negative is investigated.

testing.step: Recompute the 90-day validation clock on the sample
actions: For each sampled case recompute the validation due date as match run date plus 90 days.
Compare the disposition date recorded on the case to the recomputed due date and count days late where breached.
Confirm the comparison itself ran within 15 days of quarter end, and check the previous four quarters ran too — a skipped quarter is a market-conduct finding.
Report the on-time disposition percentage against the 100% threshold.
testing.done: validation due dates are recomputed for the sample, breaches are counted in days and quarterly run cadence is confirmed.

testing.step: Test the quality of the good-faith death validation
actions: For each sampled confirmed death open the validation evidence and confirm it is corroborating — a person report, obituary or death certificate, not just a DMF row.
For each match closed as not-a-death confirm positive evidence the insured is living, such as a subsequent premium payment, a logged conversation or an identifier mismatch that is documented.
Reject closures resting on a single undelivered letter or an unanswered telephone call.
Confirm the date of death written to the policy record matches the validated evidence, since it starts the escheat dormancy clock.
testing.done: every sampled disposition is supported by corroborating evidence and the recorded date of death agrees with it.

testing.step: Trace beneficiary location and claim initiation
actions: For each sampled confirmed death trace to the beneficiary designation in the contract file and confirm the correct beneficiary chain was applied, including contingents and assignments.
Confirm a claim packet was sent to each located beneficiary and that the claim record in the claims system is linked to the DMF case.
Check follow-up attempts at 30 and 60 days are logged where no claim form was returned.
Recompute any interest paid on delayed death proceeds from the date of death under the applicable state's prompt-payment provision and compare to the amount paid.
testing.done: beneficiary chains, claim packets, follow-ups and delayed-proceeds interest are traced and recomputed for the sample.

testing.step: Verify the handover of unclaimed deaths into the escheat population
actions: Take the list of confirmed deaths with no paid claim and match each to a row in the escheat dormancy population with the same date of death and amount.
Confirm the dormancy trigger date used in the escheat analysis is the confirmed date of death, not the match date or the claim closure date.
Identify confirmed deaths sitting in neither an open claim nor the escheat population and treat each as stranded property.
Quantify the value stranded and the report year in which it should have been escheated.
testing.done: every unclaimed confirmed death is traced into the escheat population on the right trigger date, or reported as stranded.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the policy number, platform, face amount, match category and the defect found.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list: platform not extracted, identifiers unusable, criteria too narrow, 90-day clock breached, validation unsupported, beneficiary search inadequate, escheat handover missed.
Name an owner and a remediation date, and for false negatives require a criteria change plus a back-run over the prior two years.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, for false negatives, a back-run commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute comparison coverage, on-time disposition rate and the false-negative count against the 100%, 100% and zero thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the reviewer, who sits outside claims operations and dispositioned none of the sampled matches, sign and date the workpaper.

File under Escheat / DMF / <year>-Q<n> and report coverage, false negatives and stranded property to the Compliance Committee and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for data-call readiness.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states coverage, timeliness and false-negative results, and the committee reporting date is recorded.
